text:
Alex Kim: thinking out loud — proposal to break the main enqueue into adaptive queue strata (fast, medium, slow) rather than one continuous batcher. goal: avoid SLO misses for tiny interactive requests while preserving packing for bulk.
Priya Shah: how would admission pick a strata? still preserve token affinity?
Alex Kim: selector uses a latency hint + recent per-tenant tail score. token affinity scoped inside a strata; cross-strata KV reads are read-through, writeback gated to avoid thundering.
Marco Ruiz: main worry = fragmentation. splitting lanes might create many half-full batches and regress cost. mitigation ideas?
Linh Tran: add a short "donation" window where lower-priority strata can lend headroom to faster strata for a bounded time. preserves packing but favors latency.
Samira Gomez: need clear contract: donation duration, revocation, and telemetry to validate impact.
Alex Kim: sketch of donation policy (as plain-text example): donation max duration = 20ms, donor_threshold = 60%, preemptible token cap = 8. configured per-host and per-tenant caps.
Priya Shah: KV cache warmup on strata hops is a big concern. cold KVs cause tail spikes.
Marco Ruiz: maintain per-tenant warmup credits. when a tenant moves into fast strata, spend a small prefetch budget to warm KV slots. account it in internal metrics and bill as part of a prefetch metric.
Linh Tran: observability: emit span tags: strata, donated_ms, prefetch_tokens, kv_warm_hit_rate. build p50/p95 by tenant and by model.
Samira Gomez: ops question — if fast lane saturates, autoscale it separately or flow to medium?
Alex Kim: plan: two-tier autoscale. fast lane scales aggressively (latency-sensitive slices); medium/slow scale for throughput. overflow policy: prefer_medium then slow.
Priya Shah: edge case — one tenant bursts and abuses donation, starving other fast tenants. mitigation?
Marco Ruiz: per-tenant donation caps + fairness window. circuit breaker to stop repeated excessive donations.
Linh Tran: rollout plan: feature-flagged path + metric gates: strata p50/p95, packing efficiency, token cost delta. rollback threshold: if packing cost increases >5% or tail latency regresses.
Samira Gomez: also add a runbook entry for reverting donation and forcing coalescing back into single batcher; include escalation.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: feature flag adaptive-queue-strata-v1, canary on 10% hosts, TRACE logs for strata selector for 24h.
Alex Kim: action items: build selector prototype + donation proto, add observability fields, run a 48h canary. volunteers: Marco selector, Priya cache warmup, Linh dashboards.
Priya Shah: I'll mock warmup budget and validate against replay traces.
Marco Ruiz: I'll start selector sketch tomorrow and post a PR with perf baseline.
Linh Tran: I'll wire dashboards and an eval job to replay 1M requests across tenant/model mixes.
Samira Gomez: I'll draft runbook steps after canary and include escalation steps. :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: alternate simpler option = soft-priority within single batcher. Anyone prefer that?
Marco Ruiz: test matrix should include quantized models (different prefetch costs) — donation thresholds may vary by model type.
Alex Kim: good point. include model heterogeneity in canary matrix.
Samira Gomez: noted — adding checklist item.
Alex Kim: capturing notes here. keep updates in this thread.
Marco Ruiz: quick follow-up: we should measure wasted tokens due to cross-strata boundaries (e.g., partial batches left behind). add metric wasted_tokens_by_strata.
Priya Shah: add warmup success rate and prefetch latency histograms.
Linh Tran: will include those in the dashboard. also add a small synthetic workload that exercises tiny-interactive vs bulk to observe packing curves.
Samira Gomez: final ops ask: limit feature exposure to non-prod orgs first, then a small set of low-SLA tenants before broad canary.
Alex Kim: agreed. staged rollout: dev clusters -> staging -> 10% prod hosts -> 100% if gates good.
ops-bot: checklist updated: staged rollout, metric gates defined, runbook link placeholder.
Alex Kim: thanks all — prototype time. if others have thoughts on a single-batcher soft-priority vs strata tradeoff, please post here.
